Oxford and Cambridge Society of India Scholarship (OCSI), UK 2026 is an opportunity offered by the OCSI* for Indian students pursuing undergraduate, graduate, or research programs at the Universities of Oxford and Cambridge for the 2026-2027 academic year. Scholarships of up to ₹4,00,000 will be awarded to selected students.
*The Oxford and Cambridge Society of India (OCSI) is a not-for-profit alumni organisation based in New Delhi, India.
To be eligible, an applicant must:-
be a citizen of India and ordinarily residing in India
be below 30 years old by 1st September of the application year
be a graduate of an accredited Indian university for a second undergraduate or postgraduate course (applicants graduating in the year of the award are also eligible)
be from a school in India for an undergraduate course
have applied for and secured admission to a full-time course at the University of Cambridge or the University of Oxford
intend to pursue a course of study that falls into one of the following categories:
Research leading to the Ph.D. degree
One-year postgraduate courses such as M.Phil., LLM, Diploma, CASM or Part III Maths, MBA, PGCE etc.
Taught and research-based master's programmes of various durations including M.Sc., Engineering, Medicine degree
Second bachelor's degree as an affiliated student/senior status
be admitted to the University of Cambridge or the University of Oxford through the universities' normal application procedures
Candidates are required to submit proof of admission before the scholarship is awarded and proof of residence at Cambridge or Oxford before the scholarship funds are disbursed.
OCSI doesn't guarantee admission or assist with the application process.
Selected candidates will receive the following benefits under three categories, tenable at either the University of Cambridge or the University of Oxford:-
One scholarship worth ₹1,00,000 tenable only at St. Hilda’s College, Oxford
In addition to the financial assistance, the selected candidates shall also receive:
Membership of the Oxford and Cambridge Society of India
mntoring on request by a member of OCSI
Marksheet of the previous qualifying examination

Candidates may be requested to provide details of their financial resources with supporting documents. Shortlisted candidates will be notified of this requirement. (
Financial need is not the primary criterion, it will only be considered during the scholarship selection process.)
In addition to requiring graduation from an Indian university, the OCSI scholarship program also prioritises candidates who completed their final years of schooling in India.

Candidates who have already received full financial support from other sources are ineligible to apply. If a candidate receives such support after being selected for the OCSI scholarship, they are required to inform the Oxford and Cambridge Society of India. This will allow the scholarship to be offered to the next qualified candidate.
OCSI scholars are also expected to return to India in a reasonable time frame after completing their course of study at Cambridge or Oxford.
